How long does it take to crack a password?

Average brute-force times for truly random passwords, calculated from the size of the search space. Updated November 2026.

Random passwords

Colours follow the generator's verdicts: red is very weak, green is excellent. “Letters, digits & symbols” uses the 28 symbols FortiPass generates. The generator itself shows somewhat shorter times while “Use every selected type at least once” is on: it never makes a password that misses a type, so an attacker has fewer to try.

Passphrases

Words picked at random from the 7,776-word EFF list add 12.9 bits each — about as much as two random characters, and far easier to remember. Create one with the passphrase generator.

How the numbers are calculated

A random password of length L drawn from N characters has NL possibilities, or L × log₂ N bits. On average an attacker finds it after trying half of them. The table divides that by 10¹¹ — 100 billion guesses per second, roughly what a single current high-end graphics card manages against a fast, unsalted hash such as MD5 or NTLM after a database breach. A rig of eight such cards cuts every time in the table by a factor of about ten — worth about half a character of a random password.

  • Slow hashes help enormously. Sites that store passwords with bcrypt, scrypt or Argon2 hold attackers to thousands or millions of guesses per second, multiplying every time in the table by a hundred thousand or more.
  • Online attacks are slower still. A login form that limits attempts allows a handful of guesses per minute — but never rely on that: databases leak.
  • Hardware keeps getting faster. Leave a margin. A random 16-character password has plenty.

Why your password may fall much faster

The table is for random passwords. Passwords people make up — a word, a capital letter, a year, an exclamation mark — are attacked with dictionaries and rules rather than brute force, and fall in seconds whatever their length. A password that has already leaked is cracked instantly, because attackers try known passwords first. Test yours with the password strength checker, or replace it with a random one.

Questions people ask

How long does it take to crack an 8-character password?

A random 8-character password using upper and lower case letters, digits and symbols takes about 6 hours at 100 billion guesses per second. With lowercase letters only, 1 second. A human-chosen 8-character password usually falls to a dictionary attack in seconds.

Is a 12-character password enough?

A random 12-character password with all four character types needs about 45 thousand years on average, which is enough today. With lowercase letters only, 6 days. For anything important, prefer 16 characters: 2.9 trillion years.

How long does it take to crack a 4-word passphrase?

With words drawn at random from a 7,776-word list, four words give 51.7 bits — about 5 hours. Six words: 35 thousand years.

Why do other password tables show different times?

Published tables differ mainly in the hash they assume and the hardware they count. A fast hash on graphics cards gives short times like the ones here (shorter still on a rig of many cards); a slow hash such as bcrypt gives far longer ones. The shape is the same in every table: each extra character multiplies the time by the size of the character set.

Does adding a symbol make a password much stronger?

Less than adding length. At 12 characters, going from letters and digits to all four types adds about 6.5 bits; adding two more letters or digits instead adds about 11.9.
